goldPairApprovals.note: User confirmed the reviewed pairs against the artwork and the set/card-number checklist. 2026-09-22: White Flare (SV11W) and Black Bolt (SV11B) were added - the catalog lacked their English entries, the parser read the combined Japanese expansion name ("Black Bolt/White Flare") instead of the per-printing display name, and the era filter dropped those printings. 348 distinct pairs (SV11W 162, SV11B 161, 20 cross-set, 5 promo) were checked: 0 card-name mismatches and 0 HP mismatches; the cross-set and promo groups were spot-checked against TCGdex. Ruler of the Black Flame 141/108 (Basic Fire Energy) was dropped through exclusions.json on 2026-09-19: the sample review confirmed its Paldea Evolved target is wrong. 2026-09-22 (full validation): Shiny Treasure ex was re-pointed to tcgdexSetId null - TCGdex JA has no such set (its "SV4a" is Raging Surf), so 243 EN->JA records moved to enToJa and no longer link a wrong Japanese card. 2026-09-23: 5 marketplace-only records were added for English cards whose Japanese printing has a set but no card number (SVP Paradise Resort 045/150/224 -> SV-P Promotional cards, Paldean Fates 171/186 -> Shiny Treasure ex). No exact record changed, so the artwork approvals still apply. The runtime fails closed on such a record instead of letting TCGdex guess a printing from another era (see AGENTS.md). 2026-09-23 (phase 1 of the SV coverage gap): the era now also crawls 12 English set categories, because Bulbapedia only files a page under a Japanese set category when its JP printing is that expansion, so 273 English pages had no record at all (Journey Together 52, Obsidian Flames 49, Prismatic Evolutions 34, Stellar Crown 34, Scarlet & Violet 27, ...; e.g. Journey Together 6/159 Petilil, JP Generations Start Deck Reshiram ex & Amoonguss ex 007/175). The 25 deck products those pages print are now in SET_CATALOG.ja with printsNoSetCode - Start Deck 100 Battle Collection uses TCGdex real MC id (774 cards) so its pairs validate, the rest are marketplace-only - and era-config.mjs lists them in the new extraSetNames field, because filterSourcesBySetNames keys on the Japanese set name and a deck has no category of its own (the first generate with only the English categories produced zero new records for that reason). Result: 2081 -> 2354 crawled pages, records 6127 -> 6507, enToJa 345 -> 667. Conflicts went 1 -> 18: 17 are two product lines whose numbers repeat across their member decks (ex Starter Sets 001/023 is both Alomomola and Shroomish; Stellar Tera Type Starter Sets 001/022 is both Mantine and Vulpix), which the generator drops fail-closed. The 37 new relationships were reviewed as 14 product rows with artwork and approved by the user on 2026-09-23. sm, swsh and m have the same structural gap and still need their own pass.

randomSampleReview.note: Sample cross-check of targets against live TCGdex (seed 20260301, 2 per relationship). One flag on 2026-09-22: en:SV11W:WHITE_FLARE:112/086 (Vanillish) records japaneseName バニプッチ, while Bulbapedia's own page and TCGdex (SV11W-109 バニリッチ) say Vanillish - the printed name is a source typo, the pairing itself matches on card name, number and HP, so the record is kept. The two 2026-03-02 flags are resolved: the Basic Fire Energy row was dropped through exclusions.json and the SVP 189 flag was a full-width N artifact fixed by NFKC name normalization.

fullValidationReview.note: Full pass over the era with scripts/bulbapedia/sample-review.mjs sv --all after the 2026-09-23 English-category phase (seed 20260301, live TCGdex; the 156 approved gold-pair source keys are excluded from the pool, hence 6384 of 6507). No flag is a wrong pairing and none came from the new records. 11 were a transient TCGdex HTTP 503 (SV04->SV4M 1, SV06->SV6 3, SV3->sv03 3, SV8->sv08 4); all four relationships re-checked 0 flagged on a re-run (138 / 129 / 135 / 91 records), which is the same transient-outage pattern the SWSH era hit. 4 are Japanese-name typos in the Bulbapedia source (Dedenne デデッネ, Wash Rotom ウォッシロトム, Vanillish バニプッチ twice - the English name, number and HP all match, so the records stay). 1 is a page-level HP (Pikachu SV-P 197/SV-P -> SVP 190; the page carries several printings and one shared hp while TCGdex records hp per printing).
